claims.text: The as-fabricated Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The target alloy's as-fabricated microstructure is produced by laser processing.
Direct gas-alloy interactions are the primary governor of degradation under cyclic oxidizing and reducing exposure.
Unmitigated gas-alloy interactions produce unstable and fluctuating oxide scales.
Oxidation-driven elemental diffusion and depletion contribute to degradation.
Oxide growth causes stress accumulation at the oxide/alloy interface.
Interfacial stress and elemental depletion nucleate microcracks that coalesce into catastrophic failure.
A thin, adherent Al2O3 coating acts as a diffusion barrier that suppresses direct gas-alloy interactions.
Suppressing gas-alloy interactions with the Al2O3 coating will preserve scale integrity and delay or prevent catastrophic failure.
The controlled intervention is deposition of a 50–100 nm Al2O3 coating by atomic layer deposition.
The proposed exposure alternates air and a controlled H2/N2 atmosphere at approximately 750 °C in 100-hour cycles.
Surface-layer integrity, continuity, and effective thickness modulate elemental diffusion from the alloy.
Surface-layer integrity and thickness control the formation and stability of secondary phases.
Relative to uncoated samples, coated samples will have a more uniform and stable oxide scale with smaller thickness fluctuations.
Coated samples will exhibit less elemental depletion than uncoated samples.
Coated samples will have lower microcrack density and a later onset of mechanical degradation than uncoated samples.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to conditions near 750 °C with alternating oxidizing and reducing gases and may not apply outside that window.
Long-term coating adhesion and durability under repeated thermal cycling are uncertain, and partial coating degradation could introduce additional failure mechanisms.

Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in scale fluctuations, elemental depletion, microcrack density, and mechanical degradation is proposed to falsify the direct-gas-interaction hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field recognizes that coating degradation could confound interpretation, but the falsification rule treats absence of a coating benefit as falsifying the gas-interaction mechanism without explicitly requiring that the coating remain continuous, adherent, and barrier-effective throughout exposure.
